title: UPDATE: TN, TVA partner with the United Kingdom in push to generate electricity using nuclear fusion
excerpt: The State of Tennessee has granted the first U.S. license under new Nuclear Regulatory Commission rules to develop fusion energy, enabling Type One Energy to build a 400-megawatt fusion power plant called Infinity Two at TVA’s Bull Run Energy Complex. Operations aim to start by 2034.
content:
UPDATE: The State of Tennessee and TVA are teaming up with the United Kingdom to accelerate the push toward using nuclear fusion for commercial power production as part of Project Infinity.

Officials say their partnership aims to improve supply chains and train workers to support a “safe and rapid” path toward fusion power production. This announcement follows the State of Tennessee issuing its first license to develop nuclear fusion machines to generate electricity.

As nuclear fusion moves from laboratory research to commercial use, Tennessee and the United Kingdom aim to be among the first to make the process a reality.

Tennessee’s Project Infinity and the UK Infinity Fusion Consortium are sharing resources and expertise from Type One Energy, TVA, Tokamak Energy, Oak Ridge National Laboratory, the UK Atomic Energy Authority and other partners.

TVA says its fusion licensing framework mirrors the UK Energy Act 2023.

Tennessee officials plan to break ground on Project Infinity in 2026 and have it fully operational by 2034.

Type One Energy expects startup of the project’s first phase, “Infinity One,” by 2029. Infinity One will be a prototype and workforce training center.

Type One Energy plans to create a 400-megawatt fusion power plant called “Infinity Two.” It will use stellarator technology, which uses powerful magnetic fields to confine hot plasma so fusion can occur.

The company says construction of Infinity Two may begin as early as 2028.

PREVIOUS STORY: The State of Tennessee has issued its first license to develop nuclear fusion machines to generate electricity. The fusion process is the reaction that powers the sun and stars.

This is the first license in the U.S. under the Nuclear Regulatory Commission’s new regulations for states to produce fusion energy.

Nuclear fusion is widely recognized as a limitless energy source, considered “safe” and “clean.” The Tennessee Dept. of Environment and Conservation defines the process as:

“Nuclear fusion is the process by which two or more light atomic nuclei combine to form a single, heavier nucleus. This clean process releases large amounts of energy and is the same reaction that powers the sun and other stars.”

Tennessee Governor Bill Lee and the Department of Environment and Conservation (TDEC) issued the license to Type One Energy, which plans to bring “Project Infinity” to TVA’s Bull Run Energy Complex in Clinton, Tennessee.

Officials plan to break ground on the project in 2026 and have it fully operational by 2034.

Type One Energy expects startup of the project’s first phase, “Infinity One,” by 2029. Infinity One will be a prototype and workforce training center.

Type One Energy plans to create a 400-megawatt fusion power plant called “Infinity Two.” It will use stellarator technology, which uses powerful magnetic fields to confine hot plasma so fusion can occur.

The company says construction of Infinity Two may begin as early as 2028.

“For the first time, a fusion power plant-specific licensing process has been developed and then used to grant a fusion-specific license to operate a fusion machine, consistent with a national regulatory framework for fusion energy," said Christofer Mowry, CEO of Type One Energy.  

"The importance of this milestone cannot be overstated.  Tennessee's licensing process is now the international benchmark for how to ensure fusion power plant ‘safety by design’ in a manner that can unlock the compelling economics of this transformational power generation technology. We are grateful and honored to receive this initial fusion machine license for Project Infinity," said Christofer Mowery, CEO of Type One Energy.  

TVA’s Bull Run Energy Complex was formerly a fossil fuel plant that was decommissioned in December 2023.
